Owners: database recovery owner and privacy/on-call owner. Applies to: PostgreSQL, Keycloak PostgreSQL, the independent signed deletion ledger, and the key history required to verify/decrypt retained ledger records.

This repository supplies the restore/replay mechanism, but it cannot prove a hosting provider's snapshots, WAL archive, retention, or recovery time. The release record must name the environment's measured RPO/RTO, latest verified backup ID, recovery point, storage inventory, and drill evidence. Until a real isolated restore completes this runbook, the current backup/restore gate is not passed.

Non-negotiable topology

  • PostgreSQL and Keycloak have separately restorable backups and credentials.
  • The final signed deletion-ledger volume is backed up on a recovery timeline independent of both databases. A database PITR must mount the current ledger, never the ledger snapshot from the older database recovery point.
  • Current and retained historical ledger-signing, identity-fingerprint, and provider-coordinate encryption keys are recoverable through the secret manager. They are not stored in the same backup archive as application data.
  • ACCOUNT_RECOVERABLE_BACKUP_DAYS covers every snapshot, replica, archive, export, and PITR source that can restore pre-deletion personal data. Ledger retention is strictly longer. See account-deletion.md before changing either value.
  • Backup jobs use read-only/export privileges; restoration uses a dedicated isolated target. Migration, API, worker, Keycloak, and backup roles remain distinct.

Backup verification before a release

Record an immutable backup ID in protected release values and verify all of:

  1. PostgreSQL base backup/snapshot completed and its WAL/PITR chain reaches the declared recovery point.
  2. Keycloak backup completed to a compatible point and includes realm state, clients, service-account role mappings, and user identities.
  3. The current deletion ledger and required historical keys are present in the independent inventories. Run pakperk-deletion-worker verify-ledger against a read-only copy; record both its exact canonical-record count and ledger_inventory_sha256 in the immutable inventory; never inspect or copy plaintext provider coordinates. The domain-separated digest binds the signer environment and ordered canonical signed-record envelopes, not only their count. Record an explicit zero and its environment-specific empty-inventory digest when no deletion records exist. A digest commits to the logical record set, not a storage device identity; the protected storage inventory must independently prove which physical volume or object version was mounted.
  4. Checksums, encryption-at-rest evidence, retention/expiry, region/account, and restore permissions are recorded without secrets.
  5. migration.confirmBackupId names this evidence. Do not reuse a fixture or a previous release's identifier.

Isolated restore and schema gate

  1. Create a network-isolated, non-production target with no public ingress, API, scheduled job, or deletion worker. Deny outbound identity-admin access until deletion replay is ready.

  2. Restore PostgreSQL and Keycloak to the selected points. Restore schema and data before running a newer migration. Confirm the restored database name, expected _sqlx_migrations version, and that vector, pg_trgm, and pgcrypto are each installed exactly once in the public schema. Extension name-only presence is insufficient.

  3. Mount the current independent ledger and all required keys owner-only. Set APP_ENV and ACCOUNT_DELETION_LEDGER_ENVIRONMENT_ID to the same development or staging value. The drill harness refuses production.

  4. Install a short-lived guard in the restored database. Use a unique marker that is the sanitized durable restore change ID and an expiry no more than 24 hours away. The harness also uses this exact attested and guard-bound marker as the reapply database-audit actor:

    CREATE TABLE public.pakperk_restore_drill_guard (
    marker text PRIMARY KEY,
    backup_id text NOT NULL,
    recovery_point timestamptz NOT NULL,
    restore_attestation_sha256 text NOT NULL,
    expected_ledger_inventory_sha256 text NOT NULL,
    expires_at timestamptz NOT NULL
);
REVOKE ALL ON public.pakperk_restore_drill_guard FROM PUBLIC;
INSERT INTO public.pakperk_restore_drill_guard(
    marker, backup_id, recovery_point, restore_attestation_sha256,
    expected_ledger_inventory_sha256, expires_at
) VALUES (
    'restore-CHANGE-ID',
    'backup-change-123-20260802t010000z',
    '2026-08-02T01:00:00Z',
    'sha256:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef',
    'sha256:abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789',
    statement_timestamp() + interval '2 hours'
);

  5. Ensure monitoring/admin clients are disconnected. The harness rejects any other database session. This is a point-in-time observation, not proof of network isolation; retain the network-policy evidence separately.

Migrations 12–18 release rehearsal

This is the preserved Plan 02 rehearsal contract. Before enabling any Plan 02 flag, rehearse the expand and recovery path against an isolated restore of the deployed schema-11 production-shaped backup:

  1. Retain the provider backup/PITR receipt, recovery point, schema-11 migration history, database identity, and current independent deletion-ledger inventory.
  2. Run the exact reviewed standalone migration image and DDL role once. Require migrations 12 through 18 (0012_library_v2.sql through 0018_recommendation_generation_jobs.sql) to succeed in order and every history row from 1 through 18 to have the reviewed checksum and success=true.
  3. Run the same migration command again and prove it is a no-op. Verify the v0.0-to-Inbox compatibility projection; five-state Library revisions; research-profile source separation; recommendation queue/profile/feedback fences and exact/base-identity exclusions; metadata-only search indexes; saved-query/brief/subscription/notification ownership; account-deletion cascades; interaction reason-code compatibility; retention cleanup/indexes; and absence of raw submitted titles, URLs, private notes, profile labels, feedback details, or notification payloads from operational evidence.
  4. Exercise the last schema-compatible image against the expanded schema, then re-forward to the candidate. Feature rollback keeps schema 18; never use a down migration or restore schema 11 merely to close a flag.
  5. Complete both deletion-ledger reapply and finalize below with PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_EXPECTED_MIGRATION=18, then retain the protected content IDs, backup/PITR audit records, integrity results, rollback/re-forward results, cleanup, and database/privacy/release approvals.

The repository migration tests and hermetic restore harness validate the mechanism only. This gate remains open until the provider-backed isolated restore, migration Job, current-ledger replay, and schema-compatible rollback are executed and externally anchored.

Migrations 19–24 current release rehearsal

The current Plan 03 candidate starts from the accepted schema-18 Plan 02 boundary and ends at schema 24. Before any Plan 03 switch can be enabled:

  1. Restore an isolated production-shaped schema-18 backup and retain its provider/PITR receipt, recovery point, database identity, exact migration history, and current independent deletion-ledger inventory.
  2. Run the exact reviewed standalone migration image and DDL role once. Require 0019_preparation_trigger_audit.sql, 0020_document_model.sql, 0021_passport_provenance.sql, 0022_annotations_memory.sql, 0023_version_diff.sql, and 0024_annotation_archive_import.sql to succeed in order. Every migration-history row 1 through 24 must have the reviewed checksum and success=true.
  3. Run the same migration command again and prove it is a no-op. Verify approved preparation-trigger checks and idempotency; legacy Introduction and /chat compatibility; generation-scoped document, visual, Passport, semantic, and provenance constraints; principal-scoped private artifacts and export/import bounds; account-deletion cascades; assistant expiry indexes; and stable, bounded version-diff persistence. The schema must not add a second Library or reading-feed authority.
  4. Exercise the last schema-18-compatible image that the release owner has explicitly approved against schema 24, then roll forward to the candidate. After Plan 03 writes exist, use only an image that safely ignores or understands those additive tables. Feature rollback keeps schema 24 and closes flags; never run a down migration or restore schema 18 merely to disable Deep Reader.
  5. Complete deletion-ledger reapply and finalize below with PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_EXPECTED_MIGRATION=24. Prove restored owner-bound annotations, conflicts, annotation-import ledgers, evidence cards, checkpoints, memory, assistant history/provenance, and operation rows are deleted again, while shared paper and normalized document data remain.

Repository migration and persistence tests prove only the mechanism. This gate is not_ready until a provider-backed isolated restore, exact migration Job, current-ledger replay, schema-compatible rollback/re-forward, privacy scan, and database/privacy/release approvals are externally anchored to the candidate.

Reapply and finalize

Run the first phase with the exact reviewed worker binary and the same secret files/configuration intended for the restored environment. First create a protected, owner-only, canonical JSON restore attestation. It is a closed schema: no omitted or additional members, duplicate names, non-finite numbers, multiple documents, indentation, or alternate key ordering are accepted.

{"backup_id":"backup-change-123-20260802t010000z","backup_observed_at":"2026-08-02T01:02:00Z","database":"pakperk_restore_change_123","environment":"staging","expected_ledger_inventory_sha256":"sha256:abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789","expected_ledger_records":42,"expected_migration":24,"latest_recoverable_point":"2026-08-02T01:01:00Z","marker":"restore-change-123","recovery_point":"2026-08-02T01:00:00Z","restore_completed_at":"2026-08-02T01:17:00Z","restore_started_at":"2026-08-02T01:02:00Z","schema":2,"source_revision":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567","worker_sha256":"sha256:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"}

Set its mode to 0600 (or stricter) and record its SHA-256 separately in the protected release record. The guard row must contain that same digest, backup ID, and recovery point. Recovery points use canonical whole-second UTC precision; a fractional database value is rejected rather than silently truncated. The attestation must complete within the previous 24 hours, and its chronology must satisfy recovery_point <= latest_recoverable_point <= backup_observed_at <= restore_started_at < restore_completed_at.

APP_ENV=staging \
ACCOUNT_DELETION_LEDGER_ENVIRONMENT_ID=staging \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_CONFIRM=isolated-nonproduction-restore \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_PHASE=reapply \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_DATABASE=pakperk_restore_change_123 \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_MARKER=restore-change-123 \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_EVIDENCE_DIR=/secure/evidence/change-123-reapply \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_EXPECTED_MIGRATION=24 \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_EXPECTED_LEDGER_RECORDS=42 \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_EXPECTED_LEDGER_INVENTORY_SHA256=sha256:abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789 \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_SOURCE_REVISION=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_WORKER_SHA256=sha256:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_BACKUP_ID=backup-change-123-20260802t010000z \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_RECOVERY_POINT=2026-08-02T01:00:00Z \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_RPO_SECONDS=120 \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_RTO_SECONDS=900 \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_ATTESTATION=/secure/restore/change-123-attestation.json \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_ATTESTATION_SHA256=sha256:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef \
PAKPERK_DELETION_WORKER_BIN=/usr/local/bin/pakperk-deletion-worker \
./scripts/drill_backup_restore.sh

Replace every illustrative revision, digest, backup ID, recovery point, and measured objective with the immutable values from the approved restore record. The revision must equal the clean checked-out HEAD; the worker must be an executable regular non-symlink file whose SHA-256 matches the reviewed digest. Backup IDs reject placeholder/fixture shapes. Recovery points must be valid UTC timestamps. RPO is independently calculated as backup_observed_at - recovery_point; RTO is calculated as restore_completed_at - restore_started_at. The supplied bounded integer values must equal those calculations exactly. latest_recoverable_point records the observed backup chain reach, but it is deliberately not substituted for the recovery point in the actual-drill RPO calculation.

The script verifies every ledger record before mutation, runs reapply-ledger, proves the summary accounts for every verified record, checks that matching restored users are disabled, checks every ledger has a job, and writes owner-only content-addressed evidence. It also requires the exact database name, current migration, expiring guard, environment binding, isolation, and exact ledger count from the immutable pre-restore inventory. A zero count is valid only when supplied explicitly with the exact empty-inventory digest. The worker's verification and reapply digests must both equal the protected value, so a nonempty missing, stale, substituted, or same-count wrong ledger set cannot silently produce passing evidence. For an empty set, the digest still binds the declared environment but cannot distinguish two physically different empty volumes; require the separately protected storage-volume/object-version inventory. The context records this limitation as empty_inventory_digest_does_not_prove_physical_storage_identity. Keep the mounted ledger read-only and do not run append or purge operations between the verification and reapply passes. Before any advisory lock, migration, or restore-replay mutation, the standalone migration connection and every pooled worker connection force search_path to exactly public, pg_catalog, read it back, and require the effective current schema to be public. The harness does the same for each psql session. This reset occurs after PostgreSQL applies startup settings, so a DATABASE_URL options parameter cannot redirect unqualified objects into an attacker-selected schema. Before its first database snapshot (and therefore before its first public.digest call), the harness also joins pg_extension to pg_namespace and fails unless vector, pg_trgm, and pgcrypto each resolve exactly once from public. Application readiness enforces the same namespace contract. For reapply, the harness removes any inherited PAKPERK_ADMIN_ACTOR and sets it to the attested restore marker. A caller-controlled actor therefore cannot replace the durable change ID recorded by PostgreSQL. For both phases it also forces RUN_MIGRATIONS=false; the reviewed worker's exact readiness check must inspect the recovered migration history without repairing or advancing it first, including when APP_ENV=development.

The harness copies the already-read, reviewed worker bytes into private staging, binds that copy's digest, runs only the copy, bounds and privately captures its stdout/stderr, and publishes nothing on a failed run. The same-UID recovery operator remains inside the trust boundary: portable owner permissions and a local digest do not make a file immutable against a deliberately malicious same-UID process. The evidence target must be a fresh absolute path; existing targets, symlink targets, and symlinked parent components fail during protected-input preparation before any database or worker operation.

The owner-only manifest binds schema version, source revision, worker digest, restore-attestation digest, backup identifier, restored recovery point, attested RPO/RTO timestamps, migration, environment, database, marker, phase, and exact ledger count and inventory digest. The attested marker is also the database reapply audit actor. The database guard independently repeats the database, marker, backup ID, recovery point, attestation digest, and expected inventory digest. The final context records the database's observed ledger count plus the expected, verified, and (during reapply) reapplied inventory digests and requires exact cross-file equality. The hermetic self-test exercises production preflight, database snapshot, worker-summary, evidence-closure, and failure paths through fake dependencies; it does not claim that a real database or backup was restored.

Each phase also fails if any required account, paper, core-job, library, comment/safety, or deletion table is absent. Its checksummed database snapshots record row counts for users, papers, jobs, user_paper_library, library_operations, paper_comments, comment_reports, user_reports, user_blocks, the deletion ledger, and deletion jobs. Each snapshot also records local_deletion_bindings_sha256. This digest commits to an ordered canonical JSONB array under the fixed pakperk-local-account-deletion-bindings-v1 domain: every ledger operation UUID, original-user UUID, fingerprint key ID and fingerprint bytes, plus the joined job operation UUID, target-user UUID, fingerprint binding, and nullable provider binding. UUIDs use PostgreSQL's canonical text form, bytes use lowercase hex, nulls and array boundaries are explicit, and rows are ordered by operation UUID, so concatenation and ordering cannot collide. Provider issuer/subject strings never enter evidence; only their nested, domain-separated SHA-256 participates in the outer digest. Paper and core-job counts must remain unchanged across ledger verification/reapplication; account-owned counts may decrease as deletion obligations are correctly replayed.

Then permit only the restored deletion worker to reach the restored Keycloak, start pakperk-deletion-worker run, and monitor until every replayed job is completed. A provider absence is idempotent; authentication, authorization, network, semantic, and terminal failures remain release blockers. Do not open user traffic. Stop the worker and run the harness again with PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_PHASE=finalize and a new evidence directory. Finalize requires zero unfinished/terminal jobs, zero matching restored users, intact ledger verification, and no missing jobs. Reuse the identical source revision, worker digest, backup ID, recovery point, and measured RPO/RTO so the two artifacts describe one restore exercise. It also requires PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_PRIOR_REAPPLY_CONTENT_ID set to the externally anchored pakperk-restore-evidence-v2:sha256:... ID printed by the reapply phase and PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_PRIOR_REAPPLY_EVIDENCE_DIR set to the absolute directory containing that actual package. Finalize fully verifies the prior package and requires its computed ID to match, its restore-attestation bytes to be identical, its recorded_at not to follow finalize, and its post-reapply paper/core-job counts, migration, local-ledger count, and local deletion-ledger/job binding digest to equal finalize's pre-run snapshot. Finalize is read-only: every database snapshot member, including the binding digest, must be identical before and after its verification, with the exact ledger inventory represented locally and no user row matching a ledger original UUID/fingerprint, job target UUID, or job issuer/subject; unsafe active match; missing job; unfinished job; or terminal job. A deletion_pending user may exist immediately after reapply, including a provider-matched row restored under a new local UUID, but must be absent after the deletion worker finishes and before finalize. A fabricated or unavailable ID is not a chain. Both phases require recorded_at from restore completion through no more than 24 hours afterward, with the existing five-minute future-skew cap.

Offline verification repeats the same chain checks. A finalize package cannot be verified from its ID alone:

python3 -I -B scripts/restore_drill_evidence.py verify-package \
  /secure/evidence/change-123-finalize \
  --prior-reapply-evidence-dir /secure/evidence/change-123-reapply

Sample each restored data class after finalization: paper metadata and core-job records are intact; deleted Keycloak identities are absent; the same issuer/subject cannot JIT-provision; user, library, comment, block, report, draft/cache, session, and token-related application rows are absent or pseudonymized according to policy; retained moderation evidence contains no direct account reference. Record counts and keyed integrity results, never content.

Approval and teardown

Evidence must include backup/recovery IDs and timestamps, component versions, worker image digest, schema version, exact ledger count, external inventory digest, and local ledger/job binding digest, ledger verification/reapply JSON, checksums, terminal/unfinished counts, reference device/service checks, RPO/RTO, operators/change record, and privacy/recovery approvals. Never include database URLs, tokens, key material, provider coordinates, emails, handles, raw IPs, or UGC.

On success the new evidence directory contains only pakperk-restore-evidence.tar and PACKAGE_SHA256.json, both owner-readable regular files with one link. The deterministic tar contains canonical JSON and SHA256SUMS; the script reopens it, validates the closed member set, and recomputes every checksum and the domain-separated content ID before reporting success. Record that printed content ID in an append-only release system outside the runner. Local permissions and checksums detect change relative to that anchor but cannot prevent the owner from replacing both local files.

Schema-2 attestations and schema-2 packages use the pakperk-restore-evidence-v2:sha256: content-ID domain. Current tooling rejects schema-1 attestations, v1 packages, and a v1 prior reapply ID. Historical v1 evidence remains auditable with its pinned historical source revision, but it cannot satisfy or chain into this exact-inventory release gate.

The restore attestation binds a protected provider/operator statement to the database guard and result; it does not independently prove the hosting provider's backup ID, WAL reach, timestamps, or restore operation. Preserve the provider's signed receipts or control-plane audit records alongside the external content-ID anchor.

After approval, destroy the isolated database, Keycloak target, temporary secrets, and guard according to the evidence-retention policy. A successful drill does not authorize production rollback. Repeat after backup topology, retention, deletion schema, key history, provider realm, or restore tooling changes, and at the organization's scheduled cadence.

负责人： 数据库恢复负责人以及隐私/值班负责人。 适用范围： PostgreSQL、Keycloak PostgreSQL、独立的签名删除 台账，以及验证/解密保留台账记录所需的密钥历史。

本仓库提供恢复/重放机制，但无法证明托管提供商的快照、 WAL 归档、保留期或恢复时间。发布记录必须写明该环境的 已测量 RPO/RTO、最新已验证备份 ID、恢复点、存储清单以及演练证据。 在一次真实的隔离恢复完成本操作手册之前，当前的备份/恢复门禁尚未 通过。

不可妥协的拓扑结构

  • PostgreSQL 与 Keycloak 具备可分别恢复的备份与凭据。
  • 最终的已签名删除台账卷会在独立于两个数据库的恢复时间线上进行 备份。数据库 PITR 必须挂载当前台账，绝不能挂载来自较旧数据库 恢复点的台账快照。
  • 当前及保留的历史台账签名密钥、身份指纹密钥与提供方坐标加密 密钥均可通过密钥管理器恢复。它们不会与应用数据存储在同一个 备份归档中。
  • ACCOUNT_RECOVERABLE_BACKUP_DAYS 涵盖每一个能够恢复删除前个人数据的 快照、副本、归档、导出以及 PITR 来源。台账保留期严格更长。在更改 任一取值之前，请参见 account-deletion.md。
  • 备份作业使用只读/导出权限；恢复则使用专用的隔离目标。迁移、API、 worker、Keycloak 与备份角色保持彼此独立。

发布前的备份验证

请在受保护的发布数值中记录一个不可变的备份 ID，并验证以下全部 事项：

  1. PostgreSQL 基础备份/快照已完成，且其 WAL/PITR 链已 到达声明的恢复点。
  2. Keycloak 备份已完成至一个兼容的时间点，并包含 Realm 状态、客户端、服务账户角色映射以及用户身份。
  3. 当前的删除台账与所需的历史密钥均存在于独立清单之中。请对 只读副本运行 pakperk-deletion-worker verify-ledger；在不可变清单中记录其 确切的规范记录计数以及 ledger_inventory_sha256；绝不检视或复制明文 提供方坐标。该域分隔摘要绑定的是签名者环境与有序的规范签名 记录信封，而不仅仅是其计数。当不存在删除记录时，应记录一个 显式的零值及其特定环境的空清单摘要。摘要绑定的是逻辑记录 集合，而非存储设备身份；受保护的存储清单必须独立证明实际 挂载的是哪个物理卷或对象版本。
  4. 校验和、静态加密证据、保留期/到期时间、区域/账户以及恢复 权限均在不含密钥的情况下被记录。
  5. migration.confirmBackupId 用于命名此证据。请勿复用某个测试夹具 或此前某次发布的标识符。

隔离恢复与 schema 门禁

  1. 创建一个网络隔离的非生产目标环境，不含公共入口、API、计划任务或删除 worker。在删除重放准备就绪之前，拒绝出站的身份管理访问。

  2. 将 PostgreSQL 与 Keycloak 恢复到所选的时间点。在运行更新的迁移之前，先恢复 schema 与数据。确认已恢复的数据库名称、预期的 _sqlx_migrations 版本，以及 vector、pg_trgm 与 pgcrypto 是否均在 public schema 中确切地各自安装了一次。仅存在扩展名称是不够的。

  3. 以仅限所有者访问的方式挂载当前独立台账及全部所需密钥。将 APP_ENV 与 ACCOUNT_DELETION_LEDGER_ENVIRONMENT_ID 设置为相同的 development 或 staging 值。演练框架会拒绝生产环境。

  4. 在已恢复的数据库中安装一个短期防护标记。使用一个唯一标记，其取值为经脱敏的持久恢复变更 ID，且到期时间不超过 24 小时。该框架还会将这一经证明且受防护绑定的确切标记用作重新应用时的数据库审计操作者：

    CREATE TABLE public.pakperk_restore_drill_guard (
    marker text PRIMARY KEY,
    backup_id text NOT NULL,
    recovery_point timestamptz NOT NULL,
    restore_attestation_sha256 text NOT NULL,
    expected_ledger_inventory_sha256 text NOT NULL,
    expires_at timestamptz NOT NULL
);
REVOKE ALL ON public.pakperk_restore_drill_guard FROM PUBLIC;
INSERT INTO public.pakperk_restore_drill_guard(
    marker, backup_id, recovery_point, restore_attestation_sha256,
    expected_ledger_inventory_sha256, expires_at
) VALUES (
    'restore-CHANGE-ID',
    'backup-change-123-20260802t010000z',
    '2026-08-02T01:00:00Z',
    'sha256:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef',
    'sha256:abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789',
    statement_timestamp() + interval '2 hours'
);

  5. 确保监控/管理客户端均已断开连接。该框架会拒绝任何其他数据库会话。这只是一次时间点观测，并不能证明网络隔离；请另行保留网络策略证据。

迁移 12–18 发布演练

这是保留下来的 Plan 02 演练技术契约。在启用任何 Plan 02 开关之前，请针对已部署的 schema-11 生产形态备份的隔离恢复环境，演练扩展与恢复路径：

  1. 保留提供商备份/PITR 回执、恢复点、schema-11 迁移历史、数据库身份，以及当前独立的删除台账清单。

重新应用与收尾

请使用确切的、经过评审的 worker 二进制文件，以及与已恢复环境相同的密钥文件/配置，运行第一阶段。首先创建一份受保护的、仅限所有者访问的规范 JSON 恢复证明。它是一个封闭 schema：不接受遗漏或额外的成员、重复的名称、非有限数值、多个文档、缩进，或不同的键顺序。

{"backup_id":"backup-change-123-20260802t010000z","backup_observed_at":"2026-08-02T01:02:00Z","database":"pakperk_restore_change_123","environment":"staging","expected_ledger_inventory_sha256":"sha256:abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789","expected_ledger_records":42,"expected_migration":24,"latest_recoverable_point":"2026-08-02T01:01:00Z","marker":"restore-change-123","recovery_point":"2026-08-02T01:00:00Z","restore_completed_at":"2026-08-02T01:17:00Z","restore_started_at":"2026-08-02T01:02:00Z","schema":2,"source_revision":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567","worker_sha256":"sha256:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"}

APP_ENV=staging \
ACCOUNT_DELETION_LEDGER_ENVIRONMENT_ID=staging \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_CONFIRM=isolated-nonproduction-restore \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_PHASE=reapply \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_DATABASE=pakperk_restore_change_123 \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_MARKER=restore-change-123 \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_EVIDENCE_DIR=/secure/evidence/change-123-reapply \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_EXPECTED_MIGRATION=24 \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_EXPECTED_LEDGER_RECORDS=42 \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_EXPECTED_LEDGER_INVENTORY_SHA256=sha256:abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789 \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_SOURCE_REVISION=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_WORKER_SHA256=sha256:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_BACKUP_ID=backup-change-123-20260802t010000z \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_RECOVERY_POINT=2026-08-02T01:00:00Z \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_RPO_SECONDS=120 \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_RTO_SECONDS=900 \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_ATTESTATION=/secure/restore/change-123-attestation.json \
PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_ATTESTATION_SHA256=sha256:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef \
PAKPERK_DELETION_WORKER_BIN=/usr/local/bin/pakperk-deletion-worker \
./scripts/drill_backup_restore.sh

请将每一个示例性的修订版本、摘要、备份 ID、恢复点以及测量目标，替换为来自已批准恢复记录的不可变值。该修订版本必须等于干净检出的 HEAD；该 worker 必须是一个可执行的常规非符号链接文件，其 SHA-256 必须与经评审的摘要一致。备份 ID 会拒绝占位符/测试夹具形态的取值。恢复点必须是有效的 UTC 时间戳。RPO 独立计算为 backup_observed_at - recovery_point；RTO 计算为 restore_completed_at - restore_started_at。所提供的有界整数值必须与这些计算结果确切相等。latest_recoverable_point 记录的是所观测到的备份链可达范围，但它有意不会在实际演练的 RPO 计算中替代恢复点。

该脚本会在任何写入之前验证每一条台账记录，运行 reapply-ledger，证明该摘要涵盖了每一条已验证记录，检查匹配的已恢复用户是否已被禁用，检查每条台账是否都有对应作业，并写入仅限所有者访问的内容寻址证据。它还要求确切的数据库名称、当前迁移、到期防护标记、环境绑定、隔离性，以及来自不可变的恢复前清单的确切台账计数。只有在显式提供确切的空清单摘要时，计数为零才是有效的。该 worker 的验证摘要与重新应用摘要必须都等于受保护的取值，因此非空、缺失、陈旧、被替换或计数相同但内容有误的台账集合都不可能悄无声息地产生通过的证据。对于空集合，摘要仍会绑定所声明的环境，但无法区分两个物理上不同的空卷；需要另行提供受保护的存储卷/对象版本清单。该上下文将这一局限记录为 empty_inventory_digest_does_not_prove_physical_storage_identity。请将已挂载的台账保持为只读，并且不要在验证与重新应用两个阶段之间运行追加或清除操作。 在任何咨询锁、迁移或恢复重放变更之前，独立迁移连接以及每一个池化的 worker 连接都会将 search_path 强制设置为确切的 public, pg_catalog，并将其读回，同时要求生效的当前 schema 为 public。该框架对每个 psql 会话也执行相同操作。这一重置发生在 PostgreSQL 应用启动设置之后，因此 DATABASE_URL 的 options 参数无法将未限定的对象重定向到攻击者选定的 schema 中。在其首次数据库快照之前（也就是在其首次调用 public.digest 之前），该框架还会将 pg_extension 与 pg_namespace 相连接，并要求 vector、pg_trgm 与 pgcrypto 必须各自确切地从 public 解析一次，否则即失败。应用就绪状态强制执行相同的命名空间约定。 在重新应用时，该框架会移除任何继承得到的 PAKPERK_ADMIN_ACTOR，并将其设置为经证明的恢复标记。因此，调用方控制的操作者无法替换由 PostgreSQL 记录的持久变更 ID。 在这两个阶段中，它还会强制设置 RUN_MIGRATIONS=false；经评审的 worker 的确切就绪检查必须检查已恢复的迁移历史，而不先对其进行修复或推进，即便在 APP_ENV=development 时也是如此。

该框架会将已读取、经评审的 worker 字节复制到私有暂存区，绑定该副本的摘要，仅运行该副本，对其 stdout/stderr 进行有界且私密的捕获，并在运行失败时不发布任何内容。同一 UID 的恢复操作者仍处于信任边界之内：可移植的所有者权限与本地摘要，并不能使某个文件对一个蓄意的恶意同 UID 进程保持不可变。证据目标必须是一个全新的绝对路径；已存在的目标、符号链接目标以及被符号链接的父级组件，都会在任何数据库或 worker 操作之前的受保护输入准备阶段失败。

仅限所有者访问的清单绑定了 schema 版本、源代码修订版本、worker 摘要、恢复证明摘要、备份标识符、已恢复的恢复点、经证明的 RPO/RTO 时间戳、迁移、环境、数据库、标记、阶段，以及确切的台账计数与清单摘要。经证明的标记同时也是数据库重新应用审计操作者。数据库防护标记会独立重复记录数据库、标记、备份 ID、恢复点、证明摘要以及预期的清单摘要。最终上下文记录数据库观测到的台账计数，加上预期、已验证以及（在重新应用期间）已重新应用的清单摘要，并要求跨文件确切相等。该封闭式自测试通过伪造依赖项演练生产预检、数据库快照、worker 摘要、证据收尾以及失败路径；它并不声称真实的数据库或备份已被恢复。

每个阶段还会在任何必需的账户、论文、核心作业、library、评论/安全或删除相关的表缺失时失败。其校验和数据库快照记录了 users、papers、jobs、user_paper_library、library_operations、paper_comments、comment_reports、user_reports、user_blocks、删除台账以及删除作业的行计数。每份快照还会记录 local_deletion_bindings_sha256。该摘要绑定的是固定 pakperk-local-account-deletion-bindings-v1 域下的一个有序规范 JSONB 数组：其中包含每一条台账操作 UUID、原始用户 UUID、指纹密钥 ID 与指纹字节，以及关联的作业操作 UUID、目标用户 UUID、指纹绑定，还有可为空的提供方绑定。UUID 使用 PostgreSQL 的规范文本形式，字节使用小写十六进制，空值与数组边界均为显式表示，且各行按操作 UUID 排序，因此拼接与排序不会发生冲突。提供方签发者/主体字符串绝不会进入证据；只有它们经域分隔的嵌套 SHA-256 会参与外层摘要。论文与核心作业计数必须在台账验证/重新应用期间保持不变；而账户所有的计数可能会随着删除义务被正确重放而减少。

随后仅允许已恢复的删除 worker 访问已恢复的 Keycloak，启动 pakperk-deletion-worker run，并持续监控直至每一个已重放的作业都达到 completed。提供商缺席是幂等的；认证、授权、网络、语义以及终态失败均仍然会阻塞发布。请勿开放用户流量。停止该 worker，并使用 PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_PHASE=finalize 与一个新的证据目录再次运行该框架。收尾阶段要求零个未完成/终态作业、零个匹配的已恢复用户、完整的台账验证，以及没有缺失的作业。请复用完全相同的源代码修订版本、worker 摘要、备份 ID、恢复点以及所测得的 RPO/RTO，以便这两个产物描述的是同一次恢复演练。它还要求将 PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_PRIOR_REAPPLY_CONTENT_ID 设置为重新应用阶段打印出的、已进行外部锚定的 pakperk-restore-evidence-v2:sha256:... ID，并将 PAKPERK_RESTORE_DRILL_PRIOR_REAPPLY_EVIDENCE_DIR 设置为包含该实际包的绝对目录。收尾阶段会完整验证此前的包，并要求其计算得到的 ID 相匹配、其恢复证明字节完全相同、其 recorded_at 不晚于收尾阶段，且其重新应用后的论文/核心作业计数、迁移、本地台账计数以及本地删除台账/作业绑定摘要，均等于收尾阶段运行前的快照。收尾阶段是只读的：每一个数据库快照成员（包括该绑定摘要）在其验证前后都必须保持一致，且本地所表示的台账清单必须确切，同时不存在与某条台账原始 UUID/指纹、作业目标 UUID 或作业签发者/主体相匹配的用户行；不存在不安全的活跃匹配；不存在缺失的作业；不存在未完成的作业；也不存在终态作业。一个处于 deletion_pending 状态的用户，可能会在重新应用之后立即存在（包括一行以新的本地 UUID 恢复的、与提供商匹配的记录），但在删除 worker 完成、且收尾阶段开始之前，必须不再存在。伪造的或不可用的 ID 并不构成一条证据链。两个阶段都要求 recorded_at 处于从恢复完成起、最多 24 小时之后的范围内，并保留现有的五分钟未来偏移上限。

离线验证会重复相同的证据链检查。仅凭 ID 本身无法验证某个收尾包：

python3 -I -B scripts/restore_drill_evidence.py verify-package \
  /secure/evidence/change-123-finalize \
  --prior-reapply-evidence-dir /secure/evidence/change-123-reapply

在完成收尾之后，对每个已恢复的数据类别进行抽样：论文元数据与核心作业记录保持完整；已删除的 Keycloak 身份确实缺失；同一签发者/主体无法进行 JIT 即时预配；用户、library、评论、屏蔽、举报、草稿/缓存、会话以及令牌相关的应用行，均已缺失或已按策略完成假名化；保留的内容审核证据不包含任何直接的账户引用。只记录计数与带密钥的完整性结果，绝不记录内容本身。

批准与拆除

证据必须包含备份/恢复 ID 与时间戳、组件版本、worker 镜像摘要、schema 版本、确切的台账计数、外部清单摘要以及本地台账/作业绑定摘要、台账验证/重新应用 JSON、校验和、终态/未完成计数、参考设备/服务检查、RPO/RTO、操作人员/变更记录，以及隐私/恢复批准。绝不能包含数据库 URL、令牌、密钥材料、提供方坐标、邮箱、用户名、原始 IP 或 UGC。

成功时，新的证据目录中只会包含 pakperk-restore-evidence.tar 与 PACKAGE_SHA256.json，二者均为所有者可读、具有单个链接的常规文件。该确定性 tar 包内含规范 JSON 与 SHA256SUMS；脚本会重新打开它，验证其封闭的成员集合，并在报告成功之前重新计算每一个校验和以及域分隔的内容 ID。请将打印出的内容 ID 记录到运行器之外的一个仅追加的发布系统中。本地权限与校验和可以检测相对于该锚点的变化，但无法阻止所有者替换这两个本地文件。

Schema-2 证明与 schema-2 包使用 pakperk-restore-evidence-v2:sha256: 内容 ID 域。当前工具会拒绝 schema-1 证明、v1 包，以及 v1 的此前重新应用 ID。历史性的 v1 证据在其固定的历史源代码修订版本下仍可审计，但无法满足或链接进这一确切清单发布门禁。

恢复证明将一份受保护的提供商/操作人员声明绑定到数据库防护标记与结果；它并不能独立证明托管提供商的备份 ID、WAL 可达范围、时间戳或恢复操作。请将提供商的签名回执或控制平面审计记录，与外部内容 ID 锚点一并保留。

批准之后，请根据证据保留策略销毁隔离数据库、Keycloak 目标、临时密钥以及防护标记。一次成功的演练并不授权生产环境回滚。请在备份拓扑、保留期、删除 schema、密钥历史、提供商 Realm 或恢复工具发生变化时，以及按组织既定的节奏重复本流程。
